title: Slab-and-Surge Pricing Framework for Dedicated GPU Allocations
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and validate a new pricing construct for Dedicated that balances predictable committed revenue with flexible short-term scale: fixed monthly slabs of GPU-hours plus a priced 'surge' credit pool for temporary overage. Tie offering to clearly separated SLA bands and autoscale headroom policies so customers can choose economics vs. availability trade-offs.
background: Current dedicated offerings mix reserved capacity with ad-hoc burst policies but lack a simple, predictable billing primitive for customers who want deterministic monthly costs with the option to absorb short-term demand spikes without long-term over-commitment. Sales and Customer Success report confusion about quoting and trade-offs between long-term commit discounts vs. elastic needs.
goals: Create a slab-based commitment model (GPU-hour slabs) that simplifies quoting for mid-enterprise customers
Design a priced surge-credit mechanism that is transparent and caps exposure for customers while monetizing short-term elasticity
Define three SLA bands (Standard / Priority / Critical) with explicit latency-throughput SLOs and autoscale headroom behaviors
Pilot with 3 strategic accounts and measure conversion lift, churn risk reduction, and utilization efficiency
success_metrics: Pilot conversion rate >= 40% for cohorts offered slabs vs existing reserve model
Average committed utilization improvement of 12% (reduction in unused reserved capacity)
Revenue uplift from surge credits >= $50k MRR across pilot accounts after 3 months
Net change in churn signals for pilot accounts: target <= 2% reduction in churn risk score
experiment_plan: Phase 0: Internal modeling (2 weeks) - run historical tenant usage to derive slab sizes and recommended price per GPU-hour for each slab bucket
Phase 1: Pricing & legal design (1 week) - final prices, surge credit unit definition, contract clauses for overage and preemption
Phase 2: Engineering feasibility (2 weeks) - confirm billing hooks, autoscale headroom enforcement, and metrics instrumentation
Phase 3: Pilot launch (8 weeks) - 3 customers across different verticals with staged rollout and weekly checkpoints
Phase 4: A/B evaluation (concurrent) - compare matched customers offered slab+surge vs baseline reserved + ad-hoc burst
risks: Engineering effort to slice billing at GPU-hour granularity is underestimated
Customers misinterpret surge credits as unlimited burst leading to unexpected invoices
SLA banding creates sales complexity if not reflected in quoting and console UI
Legal raises data locality/audit concerns for 'critical' SLA that require additional controls
notes: We intentionally avoid the term 'burst' in public-facing docs; using 'surge credits' frames it as a paid, limited hedge
Slab buckets should map to common usage quantiles (e.g., 100, 500, 2,000 GPU-hours/month) derived from customer telemetry
Consider a grace buffer: first 10% of overage consumed annually included in slab price for enterprise sales promotion
Design console UX to show projected monthly cost at current consumption and visualized remaining surge credits
updates: 2026-03-03: Kickoff meeting with Sales and CS. Sales requests an option that locks a fixed per-GPU-hour rate for 12 months as a close-winner feature.
2026-03-05: Engineering preliminary review — confirmed billing hook exists but needs an additional aggregation job; rough estimate added to ENG-4012.
2026-03-08: Legal flagged that 'Critical' SLA will need signed SOC2 appendix and explicit audit log delivery terms. Added dependency on Legal review.
2026-03-10: Pricing model simulation completed — suggests slab discounts at 15%, 28%, 42% for ascending commit buckets to hit target ARR uplift without encouraging overcommitment.
2026-03-12: Design pinged to mock console flow for slab visibility and surge credit purchase flow. Designer assigned: Miguel Santos.
